source.text: The lowest of the slices' hottest cells: the end slice (index 0), which makes the least heat. Slice 0 of 9 (centre at 0.0212 m, heat rate 54.553 kW/m, coolant 573 K): the closed-form slab solution of that slice gives 625.0801 K at the centre. The power shape is a cosine, normalised to an average of 1 (the heat rate is per metre of height and per metre of width). The solver's slices exchange a little heat along the height, which this solution does not have, so the tolerance is the sum of: the mesh bound 5 x 37.28 K / 100^2 = 0.019 K; the axial conduction allowance 3 x 0.00134 (the estimate as a fraction of the largest rise) x 299.9 K (the largest rise of any slice above its coolant) = 1.205 K; the cosine's 41-point table, 1e-3 of the slice's rise of 52.1 K = 0.052 K; rounded up to 0.05 K (1.3 K), fixed before any run.
source.check: Second method: FEED's own per-slice closed form (src/core/closedForm.ts through axialSummary, tests/seedOracleStack.test.ts, to 1e-3 K apart from the cosine's table term), and the real solver (FEED_SOLVER=1): every check of the run passes and the solver's slice peaks are inside the tolerances.

coverage.domain: synthetic plate (meat half-thickness 4.1 mm, gap 0.08 mm, cladding 0.57 mm, constant conductivities, one face cooled at 573 K and 30000 W/m2/K) as 9 through-thickness slices over 0.381 m with a cosine power shape, 200 kW per metre of height and width on average
